passages.original: Certe non dixit : Ego sum Pater, et ego in me : sed, Ego in Patre et Pater in me : quo dicto duas haereses elisit, Sabellianam scilicet et Arianam. Patrem et Filium non esse unam personam, ut Sa- bellius : aut duas substantias, ut Arius, sed (ut fides catholica confitetur) unam substantiam et duas docuit esse personas.
passages.english: Certainly he did not say, "I am the Father, and I am in myself," but, "I am in the Father and the Father in me." By this saying he struck down two heresies, namely the Sabellian and the Arian. He taught that the Father and the Son are not one person, as Sabellius [held], nor two substances, as Arius [held], but (as the catholic faith confesses) that they are one substance and two persons.
